text: Acute monoarthritis: A presenting complaint characterised by acute monoarthritis.
Fractures: Fracture is the cracking or breaking into pieces of an object or material under the action of stress. The science of fracture is a field of study in physics, metallurgy and engineering.
Impaired function: A presenting complaint characterised by impaired function.
Muscle weakness: Muscle weakness is a lack of muscle strength. Its causes are numerous and can be divided into conditions associated with either true or perceived muscle weakness.

Polyarthritis: Polyarthritis is any type of arthritis that involves five or more joints simultaneously. It can be associated with autoimmune conditions; it may be experienced at any age and is not sex specific.

Stiffness: Stiffness or rigidity is the extent to which an object resists deformation in response to an applied force.
The inverse of stiffness is flexibility or pliability: the more flexible an object is, the less stiff it is. Other terms with related meanings are compliance and elasticity.

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), also known as motor neuron disease (MND), Lou Gehrig's disease or Charcot's disease, is a rare terminal neurodegenerative disease defined by the progressive loss of both upper and lower motor neurons that normally control voluntary muscle contraction. ALS is the most common of the motor neuron diseases. Common presenting complaints: Muscle Weakness. Associated symptoms: Early: Stiff Muscles, Muscle Twitches, Gradually Increasing Weakness. Risk factors: Unknown (90% To 95%) Or Genetic (5% To 10%). Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Associated symptoms: Bones That Break Easily, Blue Tinge To The Sclera (whites Of The Eye), Short Height, Joint Hypermobility, Hearing Loss. MG is an autoimmune disease in which individuals form antibodies that circulate in their blood, enter tissues, bind to certain proteins in the neuromuscular junctions of skeletal muscles, and thereby reduce the number or ability of these skeletal muscles to contract when appropriately stimulated by acetylcholine.
